summary_paragraph: Mr. ___ was admitted with fever, chills, and left flank pain after his percutaneous nephrostomy (PCN) tube dislodged during parasailing and was reinserted nonsterilely by his girlfriend. He was diagnosed with a PCN site infection and urinary tract infection, treated with a 5-day course of IV meropenem. His white blood cell count improved, and subsequent urine cultures showed no growth, indicating treatment success. The PCN tube was exchanged by interventional radiology, confirming proper placement and drainage. He became agitated upon discharge planning, refusing paperwork but accepting a prescription for oral fosfomycin for three doses. He declined further evaluation or treatment for his chronic left hip pressure ulcer. Follow-up was arranged with urology to discuss surgical options due to recurrent infections, and his mother was informed of the discharge plan.
